title: Open-cover short exact sequence of etale extensions by zero
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $U,V\subseteq X$ be open subschemes with $X=U\cup V$, put $W=U\cap V$, and for $T=U,V,W$ let $k_T:T\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] write $F|_T$ for its restriction, the sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules $(E\to T)\mapsto F(E\to T\xrightarrow{k_T}X)$ on $T_{\Et}$ (the inverse image $k_T^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], up to the canonical identification for an open immersion), and $k_{T!}$ for extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For $T=U,V$ let $\iota_T:k_{W!}(F|_W)\to k_{T!}(F|_T)$ be the morphism induced, by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], by the presheaf map that is the identity of $F(E)$ on every etale $E\to X$ factoring through $W$ (such an $E$ factors through $T$) and zero on the others, and let $\varepsilon_T:k_{T!}(F|_T)\to F$ be the morphism induced in the same way by the identity of $F(E)$ on every etale $E\to X$ factoring through $T$ (the counit of extension by zero). Then the sequence of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules
$$0\to k_{W!}(F|_W)\xrightarrow{(\iota_U,-\iota_V)}k_{U!}(F|_U)\oplus k_{V!}(F|_V)\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_U+\varepsilon_V}F\to0$$
is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], and its maps are natural in $F$.

source.place: Tag 0GKK, label lemma-mayer-vietoris-shriek, proof: the short exact sequence 'can be seen by looking at stalks'

proof.text: Use the presheaves $P_T=k_{T,p!}(F|_T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. The maps $P_W\to P_T$ and $P_T\to F$ in the statement commute with restrictions: when the larger object factors through the relevant open, both composites are the restriction map of $F$; otherwise their source is zero. Composing $P_W\to P_T$ with $P_T\to F$ gives the same map for $T=U,V$, namely the identity on $F(E)$ for $E$ factoring through $W$ and zero otherwise. Their sheafified composites are therefore equal, by uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Thus $(\varepsilon_U+\varepsilon_V)(\iota_U,-\iota_V)=0$, so the displayed arrows form a complex [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. This argument also covers the empty object: every sheaf has zero sections on it.

source.place: Tag 0GKK, label lemma-mayer-vietoris-shriek, proof: the short exact sequence checked on stalks; expanded as below

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ and put $A=F_{\bar x}$, using [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. If $\bar x$ lies in an open $T$, neighbourhoods factoring through $T$ suffice for computing this stalk. Indeed $T\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and for every pointed etale $E\to X$ the pointed fibre product $E\times_XT$ is another object of $X_{\Et}$, by clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], mapping to $E$ and factoring through $T$. Refining any representative or any equality of germs this way proves directly that $(F|_T)_{\bar x_T}\to F_{\bar x}$, sending a section germ to the same germ over $X$, is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], $(k_{T!}(F|_T))_{\bar x}$ is therefore $A$ if $\bar x\in T$, and zero otherwise. Its specified isomorphism sends the germ of a section $s\in F(E)$ to the germ of that same section. It follows from the presheaf maps in step 1 that $\varepsilon_T$ induces the identity of $A$ when $\bar x\in T$, and that $\iota_T$ induces the identity when $\bar x\in W$; all maps whose source stalk is zero are zero. This identifies the actual maps, rather than only the objects.

proof.text: The geometric stalk of the binary sum is the binary sum of the stalks: the stalk functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], hence preserves this finite biproduct. There are three cases because $X=U\cup V$. On $W$ the stalk sequence is $0\to A\xrightarrow{a\mapsto(a,-a)}A\oplus A\xrightarrow{(b,c)\mapsto b+c}A\to0$: the first map is injective, the last is surjective via $a\mapsto(a,0)$, and $b+c=0$ means $(b,c)=(b,-b)$. On $U\setminus V$ it is $0\to0\to A\oplus0\xrightarrow{(a,0)\mapsto a}A\to0$, whose nonzero arrow is an isomorphism. On $V\setminus U$ it is $0\to0\to0\oplus A\xrightarrow{(0,a)\mapsto a}A\to0$, again exact. Thus every geometric stalk sequence of underlying abelian groups is short exact.

source.place: Tag 0GKK, label lemma-mayer-vietoris-shriek, proof: the short exact sequence checked on stalks; expanded as below

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact] to the complex of underlying abelian sheaves. The geometric stalk functors are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]; they jointly reflect isomorphisms by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. These are precisely the hypotheses of the categorical criterion, and step 3 supplies its stalkwise conclusion. The underlying abelian sequence is consequently short exact. No quasi-compactness, Noetherian hypothesis, or finiteness of $\Lambda$ is used.

proof.text: To interpret this as exactness of the stated module sequence, use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence]: sheaves valued in $\Lambda$-modules identify with modules over the constant ring sheaf, without changing their underlying abelian presheaves. The forgetful functor preserves kernels and cokernels and all finite limits and colimits by clauses (1) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. It reflects isomorphisms: an inverse to a bijective linear sheaf map is linear, since for $y=\alpha(x)$ one has $\alpha^{-1}(\lambda y)=\alpha^{-1}(\alpha(\lambda x))=\lambda x$, and it commutes with restrictions by the same uniqueness of inverse. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact] to this single exact functor. Step 4 says its image sequence is short exact, so the sequence of $\Lambda$-module sheaves is short exact as asserted.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, and Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; constant-scalar equivalence as in lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence

proof.text: For a morphism $\alpha:F\to G$, all squares formed by the presheaf inclusions and counits commute: on an object factoring through the relevant open both routes are $\alpha_E$, and otherwise the source is zero. Sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] carries these commutative squares to commutative squares of the prescribed sheaf maps. Taking a pair with the minus sign and taking the sum also commute with $\alpha$. Thus both arrows in the sequence are natural in $F$.
